title: Properties of Materials and Mixtures
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Properties of Materials and Mixtures Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Properties of materials; separating mixtures
standard_text: Materials have properties such as strength, flexibility, melting and boiling points, and conductivity, which decide their uses. Pure substances and mixtures; mixtures can be separated by hand-sorting, sieving, filtering, decanting, evaporation, distillation, chromatography and magnetism. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Matter and Materials: Properties of materials; separating mixtures)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): properties of materials, pure substances and mixtures, and separation methods. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A mixture can be separated by physical methods.
key_sub: Choose the method from the properties of the parts.
body_html:
How to think about it

Each material has properties that decide what it is used for: steel is strong, rubber is flexible, copper conducts electricity, polystyrene insulates. A pure substance has one kind of particle and a fixed melting point; a mixture has two or more substances not chemically joined.

Separation methods use differences between the parts of a mixture: sieving and filtering (particle size), decanting (a solid that settles), evaporation (a dissolved solid), distillation (a liquid with a lower boiling point), chromatography (dyes) and a magnet (iron).

Example

How can you separate iron filings from sand?

Iron is magnetic.

Answer: use a magnet

Example

Which method separates the dyes in black ink?

Paper and water

Answer: chromatography

Common mistakes

  • Thinking filtering removes dissolved salt.
  • Thinking a mixture always looks mixed.
  • Mixing up evaporation and distillation.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the cold water in the condenser is correct?
c: It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It make the liquid boil smoothly.
items.e: The cold water in the condenser flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.

items.q: What is the principle behind filtration?
c: Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
items.e: This is how filtration works.

items.q: What is the principle behind paper chromatography?
c: Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how paper chromatography works.
